sentences.text: CAV JUDGMENT 1.

By this petition under Articles 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioners have prayed for the following reliefs :
"(A) That this Honourable Court be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, order or direction, commanding the respondents to annul the impugned decision as reflected from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.3 at Exhibit "B" to the petition as well as from the communication of respondent no.1 at Exh."H" to the petition prohibiting the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal in the State of Gujarat (B)
That pending, admission, hearing and final disposal of the present petition, this Honourable Court be pleased to stay the implementation and operation of the impugned decision on the part of the respondents as reflected from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.3 at Exhibit'B" to the petition as well as from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.1 at Exhibit H to the petition and thereupon be pleased to permit the petitioners to continue to use castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal.
(c) That this Honourable Court be pleased to award the costs of this petition to the petitioners herein And (d) That this Honourable Court be pleased to pass such other and further orders as the nature and circumstance of the case may demand."
2.

Brief facts of the case are as under :
2.1) Petitioner no.1 is an Association of Persons and petitioners no. 2 to 16 are the members of petitioner no.1 Association dealing in the business of manufacturing and processing various kinds of pulses in the State of Gujarat.

2.2) Petitioner no.1 has been recognized by the State of Gujarat as an official forum for the purpose of entering into necessary dialogue on various issues pertaining to manufacturers of various pulses in the State of Gujarat.

2.3) It is the case of the petitioners that for the purpose of protecting pulses from insects since time immemorial in the State of Gujarat as well as in several other States of the country, castor oil is used as a medium of protection in the form of coating the pulses.

According to the petitioners, after the seeds of Tuverdal are processed to bring into existence the final product called "Tuverdal" (also known as split pulses or Toordal or Arhardal or Pigeon Pea) a coating of castor oil is applied thereon which acts as a medium of protection and thereupon Tuverdal is saved from Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/

According to the petitioners, castor oil is considered as the best available medium of protection in the form of coating of Tuverdal considering the climatic conditions prevalent in the State of Gujarat and habit of the people residing there.

2.4) In the year 1985, an objection was raised for and on behalf of respondent no.2 State of Gujarat and its concerned authorities with regard to the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating for protecting Tuverdal on the ground that the same would have the effect of rendering Tuverdal as "adulterated food"
within the meaning of the provisions embodied in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "Act 1954").
2.5) The petitioners therefore, made representations before respondent no.2 and its authorities contending that castor oil is the best available medium of protection in the form of coating for the purpose of protecting Tuverdal from the attack of insects etc.

It was further submitted that there is nothing in the Act1954, which can be said to be having the effect of classifying Tuverdal with usage of castor oil as an "adulterated food".
2.6) It is the case of the petitioners that considering the representations made by the petitioners,
respondent no.2 State of Gujarat under the signatures of the Director of Food Health issued a communication stating that it has been decided as a matter of policy not to consider usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating for protecting Tuverdal as "adulterated food"
within the meaning of Act1954.
2.7)

It is the case of the petitioners that thereafter, respondent no.3 Commissioner, Food and Drug Control Department, State of Gujarat issued a communication dated 6th January, 2003 addressed to the petitioners and its members intimating that as per the instructions received by him, it has been decided to hold usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal and other items referred to therein as not permissible under the provisions of the Act 1954 and thereupon to treat Tuverdal subjected to such a coating of castor oil as "adulterated"
within the meaning of the Act 1954.
2.8) The petitioners therefore, made representation dated 10th January, 2003, before the concerned Minister of State of Gujarat explaining as to how it would be irrational to prohibit usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating on the Tuverdal followed by the representation dated 15th March, 2003.

5. Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Dhaval C. Dave assisted by learned advocate Mr. P.A. Jadeja for the petitioners submitted that castor oil is thick, with high density and it makes a better medium of protection compared to other oils.

It was submitted that as castor oil is thick and sticky in nature,
insects find it difficult to move on the Tuverdal, which in turn prevents their growth at the place where Tuverdal is stored.
5.1) It was further submitted by Mr. Dave that castor oil contains ricinolic acid which is considered as effective in preventing growth of numerous species of bacteria, yeast and moths.

It was contended that before Tuverdal is used for its ultimate consumption as food, the same is subjected to rinsing and as a result thereof, castor oil applied thereon as a medium of protection in the form of coating,
gets dissolved in water and thereupon stands removed from Tuverdal.

sentences.text: 5.3) Referring to the aforesaid definition of the word "adulterated" it was submitted by Mr. Dave that clauses (a), (c) to (g), (i), (j), (l) and (m) are concerned, same would not have any application to the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal.

It was therefore, pointed out that whether the remaining clauses (b), (h)
and (k) would come into play so as to render Tuverdal on account of such usage of castor oil as "adulterated" within the meaning thereof or not is required to be seen.

It was submitted that clause (b) provides that if the article contains any other substance which affects or if the article is so processed as to affect injuriously the nature substance or quality thereof, then only the same would be considered as "adulterated".
It was therefore, submitted that castor oil does not affect the Tuverdal in any manner as it is only a medium of protection from the insects.

Similarly clauses (h) and (k) provides that if the article contains any poisonous or other ingredients or contains any prohibited preservative or permitted preservative in excess of the prescribed limits, then only such product would be considered as "adulterated".

It was therefore, submitted that the castor oil is neither poisonous nor injurious to health and as a matter of fact in Ayurveda, as it is a matter of common knowledge to all concerned, since time immemorial that castor oil is considered as having medicinal value for certain diseases and it is often recommended for oral consumption for solving stomach disorder.

It was further submitted that castor oil is never used as a preservative upon Tuverdal and hence the question of invoking the application of the clause (k) would not arise.
5.4) It was submitted by Mr. Dave that there is a thick line of demarcation between something which is used in the form of protection and something which is used as a preservative.

Learned Senior Advocate placed reliance upon the definition of term "Preservative" as per Rule 52 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short Rules1955) which reads as under :

sentences.text: 5.5) Referring to the aforesaid definition of term "preservative" it was submitted by Mr. Dave that in order to qualify a substance as a preservative within the meaning thereof, it should possess two fold things i.e. (i) such substance should have been added to food and (ii) such substance should be capable of preventing any substance from the process of either fermentation, acidification or decomposition of food.
It was therefore, submitted that in facts of the case, castor oil is neither added in the food i.e. Tuverdal and it does not prevent in any manner Tuverdal from the process of decaying.
It was submitted that the purpose of coating Tuverdal with castor oil is only to protect it from insects.

5.6) Learned Senior Advocate thereafter invited the attention of the Court to report of Gujarat Agricultural University dated 30th/31st July, 2003 to submit that by coating Tuverdal with castor oil, prevents insects to enter into Tuverdal.

It was therefore, submitted that the impugned communications are required to be quashed and set aside permitting the petitioners to apply castor oil as coating upon the Tuverdal so as to protect it from the insects.

Without prejudice to what is stated hereinabove, I crave leave to file the detailed reply in pursuance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, as under:
a.
I say and submit that the use of Castor Oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of pulses shall amount to addition of foreign matter.

Castor oil is nonedible oil and harmful to human health and therefore its addition/coating to the pulses would render the pulses as "adulterated" within the meaning of the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Therefore the decision of the State Government of Gujarat as well as of Central Government to prohibit the use of castor oil in the form of coating in respect of pulses is correct and nonviolative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.

b. I further say and submit that the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was an Act of the Parliament enacted in the fifty fourth year of the Republic of India to make provisions for prevention of adulteration of food.

It is further submitted that the answering respondent had the mandate under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 to lay down provisions for the standards of food and the articles used in them to be in congruence with the health of an individual.

It is submitted that the prime objective of the Act and the Rules was to eliminate the danger to human life form the sale of unwholesome articles of food or food that may be injurious to health, and to curb the widespread evil of food adulteration.
It was intended to suppress the social and economical mischief, or any evil which attempts to poison, for monetary gains, the very sources of sustenance of life and the well being of the community.

It is further submitted that under the Act and the Rule the answering respondent can prohibit the manufacture,
sale etc. of articles of food which are injurious to health.
It is submitted that the answering respondent has to perform its obligations as cast upon it by the constitution.
The Act provided for comprehensive provisions under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, which were updated by the Central Government from time to time, as deemed necessary.

c. It is respectfully submitted that the standards and quality specifications were laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 in respect of about 250 articles of food and existing standards were also updated from time to time as per the requirements.
The other food articles were being examined on the basis of general safety requirement and the information provided by the manufacturer on the label of the package on the food item.

The standard for quality and other specifications for different articles of food were laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules on the recommendation of the Central Committee for Food Standards, which is a committee of experts constituted under Section 3 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The Director General of Health Services, Government of India was the exofficio chairman of the said committee and the committee further constituted the Directors of Central Food laboratories, various technical/scientific Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India

"4.
